Before being selected in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]], he played two seasons for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]] (then in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]) as well as a season with [[BC Dnipro|Dnipro]]. Len has played twelve seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). ==Early life== Len was born in [[Antratsyt]], [[Luhansk Oblast|Luhansk]], Ukraine to a mother named Yuliia, who ran track early in her life. Growing up, Len participated in [[gymnastics]] and liked watching [[Jackie Chan]] films.{{cite web|url=http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2012-09-25/sports/bal-maryland-basketball-player-alex-len-gives-first-media-interviews-20120925_1_alex-len-maryland-madness-coach-mark-turgeon|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141011091943/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2012-09-25/sports/bal-maryland-basketball-player-alex-len-gives-first-media-interviews-20120925_1_alex-len-maryland-madness-coach-mark-turgeon|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 11, 2014|title=Maryland basketball player Alex Len gives first media interviews}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/five-things-you-need-know-about-alex-len|title=Five Things You Need to Know About Alex Len - Phoenix Suns|website=[[NBA.com]] }}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-one-one-alex-len|title=Suns One On One: Alex Len|website=www.nba.com}} As a young gymnast, Len was trained by Oleksii Stepanenko, who had also trained Olympic gold medalist [[Ihor Korobchynskyi]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20130803212543/http://sport.segodnya.ua/basketball/Mama-nashego-novichka-NBA-Lenya-o-kaktusah-mede-i-nyuansah-zhizni-v-basketbolnoy-Amerike-450784.html Мама нашего новичка НБА Лэня: о кактусах, меде и нюансах жизни в баскетбольной Америке (фото)] {{in lang|ru}} He started playing basketball at the age of 13 and later attended Dnipro Higher College in [[Dnipro]], [[Ukraine]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/alex-len|title=Alex Len - NBADraft.net|website=www.nbadraft.net}} He played for the Ukraine national team at the [[2009 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] and the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where during the 2010 tournament, he was the fourth-best overall scorer, second-best rebounder, and the best shot blocker. Following the tournament, Len joined [[BC Dnipro]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]] for the 2010–11 season. ==College career== [[File:Alex Len 2012.jpg|thumb|left|Len in 2012]] Len was recruited by then Maryland assistant basketball coach, [[Scott Spinelli]]. He was the recipient of an athletic scholarship from the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] coach [[Gary Williams]], but Williams resigned after the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11 season]]. [[Mark Turgeon]] was hired to take his place. While Williams began recruiting Len, it was Turgeon and Spinelli who eventually lured him to Maryland.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/maryland/article/maryland-adds-7-foot-2-ukranian-star-alex-len-35896/|title=IMS Exclusive: Terps Add 7-Footer}} Len underachieved in his freshman year, averaging 6 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks per game, but showed lottery pick potential after serving a ten game suspension at the beginning of the year due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] amateurism issues resulting from his play with [[BC Dnipro]], a European club team from his home nation. Len opened his sophomore season on November 9, 2012, against the reigning champion [[2012–13 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]], led by ESPN's #1 player of the 2012 recruiting class, [[Nerlens Noel]]. The game was played at the brand-new [[Barclays Center]] in [[Brooklyn]]. Len overpowered Noel throughout the entire game, scoring 23 points with 12 rebounds and 4 blocks, while holding Noel to just four points, although Kentucky won the game 72–69. Following the game, there was talk{{By whom|date=January 2020}} that Len could potentially be a top 5 pick in the upcoming draft. On January 16, 2013, Len scored 10 points, including a game-winning shot with 0.9 seconds in the game, upsetting #14 [[2012–13 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|North Carolina State]] with a 52–50 win. On February 16, 2013, Len played a role in Maryland's 83–81 victory over the top ranked [[2012–13 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke Blue Devils]]. Len put up 19 points, 9 rebounds and 3 blocks, while holding Duke star senior [[Mason Plumlee]] to four points.{{cite web|url=http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=208121790|title=Alex Len Bio|access-date=October 8, 2014|archive-date=June 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628134429/http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=208121790|url-status=dead}} He went on to average 11.9 points per game in 38 total games that season. On April 14, 2013, Len decided to declare for the [[2013 NBA draft]]. He was projected to land in the lottery, with some experts projecting Len as the #1 overall pick.{{cite web|title=Terps' Alex Len to enter NBA draft|url=http://www.baltimorenewsjournal.com/2013/04/15/terps-alex-len-to-enter-nba-draft/|work=BaltimoreNewsJournal.com|date=April 15, 2013|access-date=April 15, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130419061718/http://www.baltimorenewsjournal.com/2013/04/15/terps-alex-len-to-enter-nba-draft/|archive-date=April 19, 2013|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/terrapins-insider/wp/2013/06/27/alex-lens-final-nba-mock-draft-roundup-no-1-overall-still-a-possibility/|title=Alex Len's final NBA mock draft roundup: No. 1 overall still a possibility?|first=Alex|last=Prewitt|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=June 27, 2013}} On May 3, 2013, Len ended up getting surgery on his left ankle that resulted in him being out for several months, ultimately causing him to sit out from the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9239845/alex-len-miss-all-pre-draft-workouts-surgery|title=Likely lottery pick Len out after ankle surgery|date=May 3, 2013}} ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2013–2018)=== ====2013–14 season==== Len was selected fifth overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the 2013 NBA draft. Len was the second international-born player to be selected in that draft, behind the first overall selection in [[Canada|Canadian]]-born [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]], as well as the highest-selected [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]]-born player to be drafted in the NBA, which was a record previously held by [[Vitaly Potapenko|Vitalii Potapenko]] in 1996. He was also the first Suns player to be taken in the top 5 of an NBA draft since [[Armen Gilliam]] in 1987. Due to his ankle surgeries, Len did not join the Suns for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On July 12, 2013, Len had surgery on his right ankle due to a [[stress fracture]].{{cite web|url=http://valleyofthesuns.com/2013/07/12/alex-len-undergoes-right-ankle-surgery-suns-announce/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130817164418/http://valleyofthesuns.com/2013/07/12/alex-len-undergoes-right-ankle-surgery-suns-announce/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 17, 2013|title=Alex Len undergoes right ankle surgery, Suns announce|date=July 12, 2013}} He signed with the Suns on August 29, 2013,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/first-round-pick-alex-len-signs-suns|title=FIRST ROUND PICK ALEX LEN SIGNS WITH SUNS - THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE PHOENIX SUNS|website=www.nba.com}} and was cleared to practice with them by early September.{{cite web|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/09/12/suns-rookie-alex-len-says-he-is-cleared-to-practice/|title=Suns rookie Alex Len says he is cleared to practice|date=September 12, 2013}} Len made his NBA debut on November 1, 2013, at home in a close victory against the [[Utah Jazz]]. He sat out seven games before returning on November 19 against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. However, a day later, Len re-injured his left knee and missed over six weeks before returning on January 7 against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Len had his first 10-rebound game in a 126–117 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on January 29, 2014.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lenal01/gamelog/2014/|title=Alex Len 2013-14 Game Log - Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ====2014–15 season==== In July 2014, Len joined the Phoenix Suns for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. In the Suns' first game of the Summer League, Len recorded 6 points and 6 rebounds against the [[Golden State Warriors]] before fracturing his right pinkie finger and was subsequently ruled out until training camp.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11210527/alex-len-phoenix-suns-miss-rest-summer-league-broken-pinky|title=Suns' Len (finger) out of summer league|date=July 13, 2014}} On October 7, 2014, a day before the Suns' first pre-season game of [[2014–15 NBA season|2014]] against Brazilian club [[Flamengo Basketball|Flamengo]], Len fractured the same pinkie finger again, forcing him to the sidelines once more.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/len-sidelined-fractured-finger|title=Len Sidelined With Fractured Finger - Phoenix Suns|website=[[NBA.com]] }} He returned to action two weeks later in the Suns' pre-season game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on October 22.{{cite web|url=http://www.csnbaltimore.com/ncaa-maryland-terps/alex-len-makes-one-big-play-return-nba-court|title=Alex Len makes one big play in return to NBA court|access-date=October 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141025030832/http://www.csnbaltimore.com/ncaa-maryland-terps/alex-len-makes-one-big-play-return-nba-court|archive-date=October 25, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} On October 31, 2014, Len recorded his first career double-double with career-highs in points and rebounds with 10 and 11, respectively, in the Suns' 94–89 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141031/SASPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Spurs at Suns|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 1, career-high 19 points in a 118–114 win over the Boston Celtics.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141117/PHXBOS/gameinfo.html|title=Suns at Celtics|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 18, Tucker with 24 points (prev. 23, 3/14/16) and @alexlen with 7 assists (prev. 6, 3/6/16) #SunsAtRockets|first=Phoenix Suns|last=Stats}} Len appeared in 78 games for the Suns in 2015–16, starting in 46 of them, both career highs. He recorded 19 double-doubles and finished with averages of 9.0 points, 7.6 rebounds and 1.2 assists, all career highs. ====2016–17 season==== [[File:Partido NBA -i---i- (32286841595) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Len preparing to shoot a free throw in January 2017]] After going 0–4 to start the season, Len helped the Suns record their first win on November 2 with 18 points in a 118–115 overtime victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899513|title=Bledsoe's 3 sinks Blazers in OT, 118-115|work=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2016}} On November 8, he recorded 16 points and a season-high 14 rebounds in a 107–100 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899563|title=Bledsoe, Dudley lead Suns past Pistons 105-99 [sic]|work=ESPN.com|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 9, 2016}} On December 9, he recorded 14 points, 13 rebounds and a season-high five blocks off the bench in a 119–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899786|title=Eric Bledsoe scores 30, Suns hold off Lakers 119-115|work=ESPN.com|date=December 9, 2016|access-date=December 10, 2016}} On February 10, 2017, he was suspended one game without pay for leaving the bench area and entering the playing court during an altercation in the Suns' 110–91 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] two days earlier.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/02/10/phoenix-suns-alex-len-suspended-one-game-leaving-bench|title=Suns' Len suspended one game for leaving bench during altercation|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2017|access-date=February 10, 2017}} ====2017–18 season==== Following the 2016–17 season, Len became a restricted free agent. On September 25, 2017, after spending the off-season looking to get a better deal,{{cite On September 16, 2025, Len signed an Exhibit 9 contract with the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web|title=New York Knicks Sign Alex Len To An Exhibit 9 Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-alex-len-to-an-exhibit-9-contract|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} He was waived by the Knicks prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.{{Cite web|title=Knicks officially release Alex Len, Garrison Matthews and Matt Ryan|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/knicks-officially-release-alex-len-210559564.html|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} ===Real Madrid (2025–2026)=== On October 30, 2025, Len signed a multi-year contract with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |title=Real Madrid reels in 12-year NBA veteran Alex Len |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/de/euroleague/news/real-madrid-reels-in-12-year-nba-veteran-alex-len/ |date=2025-10-30 |access-date=2025-10-31 |website=euroleaguebasketball.net |language=en}} On November 7, Len made his team debut in a 101–92 win against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]] in the [[2025–26 EuroLeague regular season|EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |title=Real Madrid reels in 12-year NBA veteran Alex Len |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/de-DE/news/basket/erste-mannshaft/latest-news/alex-len-debuta-con-el-real-madrid-07-11-2025 |date=2025-11-04 |access-date=2025-11-11 |website=realmadrid.com |language=en}} He played in 40 games for the team (21 games in the [[2025–26 ACB season|League ACB]], 19 games in the [[2025–26 EuroLeague|EuroLeague]]),{{Cite web|title=Profile of Alex Len at basketball-reference.com|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/alex-len-1.html|access-date=August 11, 2026|website=basketball-reference.com|language=en}} logging averages of 3.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 0.9 blocks. On July 7, 2026, Len and Real Madrid parted ways.{{Cite web|title=Former Lakers center leaves Real Madrid after short stint|url=https://basketnews.com/news-251573-alex-len-leaves-real-madrid-after-short-stint.html|access-date=August 11, 2026|website=basketnews.com|language=en}} ==National team career== Len played for [[Ukraine national basketball team|Ukraine]]'s Under-16 national team during the [[2009 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]. Despite his performance throughout the tournament, which included a 20-point outing against [[Israel national basketball team|Israel]] and averaging 8.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and being the second-best shot blocker in the tournament with 2.6 blocks per game,{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.playerID_75836.compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2009.roundID_6650.teamID_2183.html|title=Oleksii Len - U16 European Championship Men (2009) - FIBA Europe|website=www.fibaeurope.com}} the Under-16 national team was relegated under the Division B section after the tournament for over a year's time. He played with his nation's Under-18 national team for the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. Unlike in the Under-16 Tournament he participated in back in 2009, Len helped the Under-18 team stay in the Division A tournaments for at least another year. His performance throughout the tournament led to the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|University of Maryland]], along with a few other universities like [[Virginia Tech]], gaining enough interest in him to get him on their team. In August 2018, Len was named to play for the [[Ukraine national basketball team]] for the first time at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification|2019 FIBA World Cup qualifiers]] in September.{{Cite web |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/national-teams/national-teams/286823/alex-len-and-svi-mykhailiuk-will-be-available-for-ukraine-at-next-fiba-wc-qualifier-window.html |title=Alex Len and Svi Mykhailiuk will be available for Ukraine at next FIBA WC qualifier window |access-date=September 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181005015030/https://sportando.basketball/en/national-teams/national-teams/286823/alex-len-and-svi-mykhailiuk-will-be-available-for-ukraine-at-next-fiba-wc-qualifier-window.html |archive-date=October 5, 2018 |url-status=dead }} Throughout the qualifiers, he averaged approximately 10.5 points, 6 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game, playing a key role as the team's starting center. His presence was important in Ukraine's competitive performances to qualify for the World Cup. Len has continued to represent Ukraine in subsequent international competitions, further establishing himself as a core player for the national team.{{Cite web |date=2025-10-26 |title=Alex Len
